title: Children and animals may have coarser awareness without a mature prefrontal cortex

statements.text: How fine-grained awareness is in children and animals is open, and coarser awareness might not need a fully developed prefrontal cortex. Self-referential conscious thinking needs third-order states that may be absent in small children and animals, but awareness does not need it, and rats and dolphins show sensory metacognition.

sources.quote: it is an open question how fine-grained conscious awareness is in children and animals, and less fine-grained awareness might not require a fully developed prefrontal cortex
Signs of sensory metacognition have been observed in animals such as rats and dolphins
